title: How accurately can soft error impact be estimated in black-box/white-box cases? - a case study with an edge AI SoC -
problem: Determining how accurately soft error impacts can be estimated in edge AI SoCs through simulation in both white-box (self-designed with full access) and black-box (commercial off-the-shelf with limited access) scenarios. The challenge is validating whether pre-silicon assessment can predict post-silicon reliability measured via physical testing.
motivation: Edge AI devices with numerous storage units and sequential logic are vulnerable to soft errors, and accurate pre-deployment reliability assessment is critical for reliable edge AI applications.
method: Uses alpha particle irradiation results on a 22nm AI SoC as a golden reference. Performs fault injection across the entire chip in white-box simulation and into accessible memory/registers in black-box simulation. Compares simulation results between both approaches and against physical irradiation data to validate consistency.
key_novelty: Demonstrates that white-box pre-silicon reliability assessment through comprehensive fault injection achieves high consistency with actual alpha particle irradiation, and that black-box assessment yields comparable results when memory-to-register proportions are preserved.
contributions: Validation that pre-silicon white-box reliability assessment is feasible and accurate versus physical alpha particle irradiation
Empirical evidence that black-box simulation with restricted access provides reasonable soft error estimates
Demonstration that memory dominance in soft error profiles makes black-box and white-box results comparable
Practical methodology for reliability assessment applicable to both custom-designed and commercial SoCs

metrics.accuracy: consistency between white-box/black-box simulation and alpha particle irradiation soft error impact estimates
metrics.other: soft error rate, memory vs register failure contribution proportion

baselines: alpha particle irradiation on 22nm AI SoC
limitations: Generalizability across different SoC architectures with varying memory-to-register ratios is not addressed; evaluation limited to single 22nm AI SoC design.
primary_theme: soft error reliability characterization for edge AI SoCs
